objective:
Where could software create a meaningful baseball advantage for the Chicago Cubs?

Do not assume the product. Explore different opportunity classes: different users inside a baseball organization (front office, scouting, player development, coaching, medical/performance staff, analysts, game-day staff), different recurring decisions, and different mechanisms of value (better information, faster combination of signals, reduced costly uncertainty, process reliability, avoided errors). Include boring-but-useful interventions and non-obvious possibilities. Also name places where software is unnecessary because a spreadsheet, an existing public tool, or a manual process already suffices, and places where sophisticated clubs likely already have the advantage.

OUTPUT GUIDANCE (format only): Each IDEA line names one distinct baseball problem, the intended user, the concrete repeated decision, and the software intervention. Follow each IDEA with ASSUMPTION lines for what must be true (including whether lawfully accessible public data could support it) and UNKNOWN lines for missing evidence. Do not invent statistics or private Cubs information (scouting, medical, biometric, contract, or proprietary tracking data).
text: IDEA: Calibration tool for minor league call-ups, for analysts and the front office. The repeated decision is whether a minor leaguer is ready to be promoted. The software would translate public minor league stats into MLB-equivalent estimates with explicit uncertainty bands, not just a single number.

claims.text: Calibration tool for minor league call-ups, for analysts and the front office. The repeated decision is whether a minor leaguer is ready to be promoted. The software would translate public minor league stats into MLB-equivalent estimates with explicit uncertainty bands, not just a single number.

assumptions: The Cubs' home day-game share differs enough from league norms that turnaround stress matters. This must be verified from public schedules, not presumed.
Schedule-only features carry a real signal about fatigue or performance without private sleep or biometric data. That signal may be weak or confounded by which teams are good.
Staff already handle this by feel, so the tool's value may be only reliability and reminders rather than new information.
Errors or missed flexibility in this area happen often enough to matter. The challenge is that a well-kept spreadsheet plus a rules-literate staffer may already be enough.
Option and service status can be reconstructed from public transaction logs. Edge cases such as injured-list time and rule changes may not be fully public.
Public transaction feeds and public performance data update fast enough for the claim window.
Sophisticated clubs likely already run this, so any edge would come from faster internal routing to decision-makers, not from better data.
Tipping is common enough and detectable from consistent camera angles. Broadcast video may be too inconsistent to rely on.
Running the tool only on the club's own pitchers and only off-field keeps it within MLB rules on electronic equipment. Downstream compliance review would be needed.
A sharp-eyed coach watching video may already catch most tells, which limits the software's marginal value.
Hidden workload such as "warmed up but not used" is under-tracked today. Public data does not capture it, so staff would need to enter it manually.
A whiteboard or shared sheet may already be sufficient. Software only helps if it is used more consistently than those.
This is distinct from wind-based positioning. The value lies in protecting starters and avoiding lost innings, not in fielding alignment.
Delay timing is partly controlled by the league or umpires once the game begins, which limits the club's leverage to the pregame period.
Contradictory coaching after promotions actually happens and slows development. This is plausible but unverified.
Sophisticated clubs likely already have player-plan systems, so the opportunity may be in adoption rather than invention.
Communication friction measurably delays adjustments. Human interpreters may already handle this well, and machine translation of baseball jargon may introduce errors.
The value comes from avoided errors under time pressure, not new insight. Printed cards made from a spreadsheet may already capture most of it.
Public splits are noisy at small samples, so the cards would need regressed estimates or they risk false precision.
Staff would record honest predictions in advance. Organizational incentives may discourage this.
Feedback loops are long, measured in years, so the benefit is slow and hard to attribute.
Public minor league tracking data is rich enough. Much of the best minor league data may be private or uneven across levels.
Sophisticated clubs likely already hold better translation models, so a public-data version would be a baseline only.
Public data reliably records disengagements. If it does not, staff would need to tag them manually.
Most clubs already exploit this rule, so any edge has likely narrowed since the rule was introduced.
Pool rules and amounts are public. Prospect evaluations would be private and must not be invented, so the tool would only be a scenario shell.
A spreadsheet likely suffices unless rules or trade options are complex.
Public reporting on arbitration filings and outcomes is complete enough.
Clubs and agencies already maintain such databases, so the advantage is likely small.
Those public tools remain available and permitted for club use.
The Cubs have in-house capability in these areas. This is not established and must not be presumed without evidence.

Day-game rest planner for medical/performance staff. The repeated decision is which regulars get a day off or a lighter pregame workload after a night game followed by a day game. The software would turn the public schedule, travel legs and start times into a "turnaround stress" flag for each series.
public_evidence_day_after_night_performance_effect
cubs_current_rest_day_process

Roster-rules ledger for front office operations. The repeated decision is optioning, recalling, DFA timing, 40-man protection and Rule 5 eligibility. The software would track option years, the days a player must stay down after being optioned, and eligibility deadlines, then warn before a move becomes impossible or costly.
cubs_roster_admin_error_history
completeness_of_public_option_status_data

Waiver and DFA market monitor for the front office. The repeated decision is whether to claim, trade for, or pass on a player designated by another club. The software would rank newly available players against the Cubs' 40-man needs within the claim window.
typical_decision_latency_on_claims

Own-pitcher tip self-audit for coaching and player development. The repeated decision is which mechanical tells to fix between starts. The software would compare a pitcher's set position, glove and timing by pitch type using the club's own video, outside games, to find tells opponents could read.
rate_of_detectable_tipping_in_mlb_pitchers
video_angle_consistency_available_to_club

Bullpen readiness ledger for the coaching staff. The repeated decision is which relievers are truly available tonight. The software would log warm-ups that never led to a game appearance, back-to-back days and high-stress innings in one shared view for the manager and pitching coach.
cubs_bullpen_tracking_practice
evidence_linking_unrecorded_warmups_to_injury_or_performance

Rain-delay and start-time decision support for game-day staff and the manager. The repeated decision is whether to start the starting pitcher, delay, or switch to a bullpen game when rain is forecast. The software would combine public radar nowcasts with the starter-reentry risk after a delay.
frequency_of_weather_affected_cubs_home_games
club_vs_league_authority_over_start_time

Shared development-plan record for player development across minor league affiliates. The repeated decision is which cue or drill a player works on this week. The software would keep one plan per player that every coach sees, so a player promoted between affiliates does not receive contradictory instruction.
cubs_existing_player_plan_tooling
measurable_effect_of_cue_consistency_on_development

Multilingual plan delivery for player development and coaching. The repeated decision is how to communicate daily plans to international and Spanish-speaking players. The software would deliver plans as reviewed translations with short video, rather than through ad hoc interpretation.
player_reported_communication_gaps

Pre-game decision cards for the manager and bench coach. The repeated decision is pinch-hitting, platoon and double-switch choices in late innings. The software would precompute the bench options matchup by matchup before first pitch, so in-game choices become a lookup.
frequency_of_suboptimal_late_inning_choices

Decision journal and calibration log for front office and analysts. The repeated decision is any forecast-based call: trades, call-ups, or draft picks. The software would record each forecast and its confidence before the decision, then score those forecasts later to show where staff judgment is over- or under-confident.
existing_cubs_decision_review_process

Calibration tool for minor league call-ups, for analysts and the front office. The repeated decision is whether a minor leaguer is ready to be promoted. The software would translate public minor league stats into MLB-equivalent estimates with explicit uncertainty bands, not just a single number.
public_milb_statcast_coverage_by_level

Baserunning disengagement exploiter for coaching. The repeated decision is when to attempt a steal or take a larger lead given how many pickoffs and step-offs (disengagements) the pitcher has already used. The software would show live opponent disengagement counts and each pitcher's tendency after reaching the limit.
public_disengagement_data_availability
current_league_wide_steal_success_trend

International signing pool allocator for the front office and international scouting. The repeated decision is how to spread the bonus pool across prospects and whether to trade for extra pool space. The software would model budget scenarios against signing deadlines.
current_international_signing_rules_status

Arbitration comparables finder for the front office. The repeated decision is filing numbers and whether to settle or go to a hearing. The software would retrieve public past arbitration outcomes and similar players.
completeness_of_public_arbitration_records
Not worth building: custom public leaderboards and basic split lookups. Existing public tools such as Baseball Savant and FanGraphs already serve analysts for routine queries.
Likely already covered at sophisticated clubs: pitch design, biomechanics labs, and defensive positioning models. New software here would compete with mature systems and probably add little.
cubs_internal_analytics_capabilities

hard_constraints: Do not assume the problem or the solution.
Use only lawfully accessible public, historical, or clearly labeled synthetic data.
Do not invent private Chicago Cubs information or statistics.
Distinguish fact, assumption, hypothesis, and speculation.
provenance.unit_selection_scope: Single IDEA line; batch assumptions/unresolved issues retained without claim-specific association. Parent rejection/contradiction gates retained.
